answer: Each live key may hold only one licensed tide-gauge berth on a mapped headland knoll, from a hard yearly cap. Enrollment binds the berth and a sealed harbor lantern—whose flicker fingerprint cannot be copied—to a single signing key, then locks a serial-tagged cultured pearl in escrow. Audits require a signed photometry of that lantern at a random hour; peers recompute intensity and timing, and they forfeit the pearl if a second key appears on the same berth. Every alias therefore needs its own knoll, lantern, and pearl, so attacker cost grows at least linearly.
